title: Eve wasn’t tempted by evil—she was tempted by something that looked good (Genesis 3:6)
paragraphs: Eve wasn’t tempted by evil—she was tempted by something that looked good (Genesis 3:6)

Eve wasn’t pulled by something ugly.
She was drawn to something appealing.
“Good for food… pleasing to the eyes… desirable” (Genesis 3:6).

Sin rarely walks in wearing chains.
It often comes dressed like wisdom.
Like opportunity.
Like freedom.
Like something you “deserve.”
And that is still how temptation works.

The enemy does not always tempt you with what is obviously wicked. He tempts you with what looks good without God. A relationship that feels right but rebels against holiness. An ambition that shines but chokes surrender. A desire that looks harmless until it asks you to distrust the Word of God.

The first temptation was not just about eating fruit.
It was about redefining good and evil apart from God.
That same poison still runs through the human heart. We want the blessing without the boundary. The promise without the Provider. We reach for what looks good, and in the reaching, we fall.
But praise God—Genesis 3 is not the end of the story.

Where Adam and Eve failed in a garden, Jesus overcame in the wilderness. Where the first humans grasped, Christ surrendered. Where sin entered through deception, grace entered through the cross. Jesus did not come merely to make bad people behave better. He came to rescue blind hearts that keep calling dangerous things beautiful.

So yes—be careful with obvious evil.
But be even more careful with what looks good if it leads you away from God.

Not everything attractive is holy.
Not everything desirable is safe.
Not everything “good” is God.
And that’s where grace walks in.

If you have already bitten into something that looked beautiful and left you broken, come to Christ. There is mercy for the deceived. There is cleansing for the ashamed. There is restoration for those who finally admit, “Lord, I wanted what looked good more than I wanted You.”

Jesus still receives repentant sinners.
Jesus still covers naked shame.
Jesus still calls us back.
